findings.title: The specification advertises an unencrypted HTTP server
findings.summary: At least one declared server uses HTTP. The specification does not prove whether HTTPS is also configured or enforced.
findings.impact: Traffic sent over plain HTTP can be read or modified by parties on the network path.
findings.remediation: Prefer HTTPS for API traffic and redirect or reject plaintext HTTP at the service boundary.

findings.title: A response schema contains a potentially sensitive field
findings.summary: A response schema uses a field name commonly associated with secrets or personal data. This heuristic may flag legitimate fields and does not inspect live responses.
findings.impact: If the field contains a real secret or sensitive value, returning it to an unintended caller could expose data.
findings.remediation: Review the field and access policy. Omit secrets from responses, and mark request-only fields as writeOnly where appropriate.

findings.title: A request or collection response lacks documented resource bounds
findings.summary: Request strings or maps lack schema limits, or a GET response returns a top-level array without a recognizable pagination parameter. These are contract review hints and do not establish runtime resource exposure.
findings.impact: Large request values or unbounded collection responses can increase memory, CPU, and downstream load when runtime limits are also absent.
findings.remediation: Document realistic maxLength and maxProperties values, enforce request limits in the service, and paginate large collection endpoints.
